subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose scoped ACP permission defaults as generic `permissionProfile` values, ACPX-specific `permissionMode` and `nonInteractivePermissions` values, or no static scoped permission defaults?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes which channel-bound headless sessions receive write and shell authority and could create a parallel public config surface.

options.title: Use generic scoped permission profiles
options.body: Add per-agent and per-binding `permissionProfile` defaults that flow through the existing ACP runtime option layer while keeping ACPX `permissionMode` plugin-global.

options.title: Add ACPX-specific scoped keys
options.body: Implement the requested `permissionMode` and possible `nonInteractivePermissions` precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific public config contract.

options.title: Keep global-only permissions
options.body: Document global ACPX permissions plus live `/acp permissions` controls as the supported paths and leave static scoped defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use generic scoped permission profiles
recommendation.body: Add per-agent and per-binding `permissionProfile` defaults that flow through the existing ACP runtime option layer while keeping ACPX `permissionMode` plugin-global.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the ACP runtime option shape and ACPX integration history most directly tied to the durable permission contract.
